model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x FFO margin less maintenance/leasing capex = AFFO; net debt NOT deducted)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 statutory revenue (Dec-25 year, A$m: rent 815.8 + property/investment/development management fees + development revenue). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow that is valued is FFO (63.0% of revenue in FY2025, 62.3% in FY2024) less maintenance and leasing capex, i.e. AFFO as GPT defines it under the PCA guidelines. Revenue and FFO have moved together (FFO/revenue 63.0% FY25, 62.3% FY24), so the growth path is applied to revenue and read as FFO growth.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,915,577,430 stapled securities on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (unchanged since 2021) plus 4.8m performance security rights at weighted-average basis = 1,918.3m diluted WANOS (H1 FY2026 interim, EPS note (d)). Held FLAT: no buybacks (the A$3-6m/yr 'purchase of treasury securities for employees' funds the rights, not a buyback), no DRP in operation, no raise assumed in base.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow discounted is AFFO, which is already AFTER net finance costs (FY2025 A$219.7m; FY2025 finance costs paid A$219.5m). Deducting the A$5,434m balance-sheet net debt (5,554.5 borrowings - 120.3 cash at 30-Jun-2026) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never capitalise a post-interest flow and then subtract net debt). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit only. Net gearing 31.5% at 30-Jun-2026 (target range 25-35%), covenant gearing 32.0% vs 50% limit, ICR 4.0x vs 2.0x covenant, liquidity A$1,029m, WADE 4.2 years.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO (A$m): FFO 650.5 less maintenance and leasing capex 156.1 = 494.4 (FY25 AR p.1051), 25.8 cps. This is the owner flow the valuation capitalises. NOT the CSV free_cash_flow of 380.7 (OCF 622.1 - capex 241.4, which includes development/growth capex on the ~A$3bn logistics pipeline and Rouse Hill/Melbourne Central redevelopments) and NOT GPT's own 'free cash flow' of 479.5 (AFFO after working-capital timing).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 FFO (Funds From Operations, PCA definition), 34.0 cps, +5.5% on FY2024's 616.3. Statutory NPAT (981.0 in FY2025, -200.7 in FY2024) is dominated by investment-property revaluations (+310.0 / -770.7) and is not used anywhere in this valuation.
inputs.sbc_source: Security-based payment expense (A$4.2m FY2022, FY25 AR employee-benefits note) is expensed inside FFO and NOT added back, so no second deduction is made; the performance rights it grants (4.8m) are in the diluted count. FY2025 AR discloses no cash-flow SBC add-back line. House and street bases therefore coincide (SBC-zero convention).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest received A$6.1m is left inside FFO (it nets within the A$219.7m net finance cost line) because net debt is not deducted and no cash is added to EV: the excluded-income/matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T06:10:04Z (ASX regular close 16:10 AEST; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 4.375-5.75)
inputs.nta_note: NTA A$5.61 at 30-Jun-2026 (A$5.53 Dec-25, A$5.27 Dec-24, A$6.09 peak Dec-21). The current_price is ~0.80x NTA. Recorded as a cross-check only; the valuation is earnings-based because NTA carries the valuers' cap rates (Office 6.26%, Retail 5.41%, Logistics 5.61%), not the house cost of equity.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and no net debt is deducted: AUD 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.6% (Sep-2026; ~4.5-4.7% through 2025 per FY25 AR) + 0.9 beta x 5.0% Australian ERP = 9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows). Cross-check: at the current_price (inputs.price_as_of) the market capitalises FY2026E AFFO of ~26.7 cps at a ~5.9% AFFO yield, i.e. an implied cost of equity of ~8.4-8.9% for 2.5-3.0% growth -- the house rate sits ~0.5pp above what the price implies.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground and other property lease liabilities (A$30.2m at Dec-25) are immaterial and are inside FFO as an expense; no separate lease charge and no lease liability in the (zero) net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; FFO is attributable to stapled securityholders. Co-investment income from GWSCF/GWOF/GQLT is equity-accounted and already inside FFO.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row (IAS 40 fair-value property trust; statutory NPAT is revaluation noise, EBITDA undefined, reported FCF includes growth development capex). Run on the Drivers/engine route, CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin = FFO margin (post-interest, post-tax: FY2025 income tax on the management company A$15.8m is already deducted inside FFO, so cash_tax_rate = 0), D&A = 0 (investment property is not depreciated under IAS 40; PP&E depreciation A$4.6m is inside FFO), SBC = 0 (expensed inside FFO), capex = maintenance and leasing capex (the FFO-to-AFFO bridge), working capital = 0, net_debt = 0. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the 22-Sep-2026 ASX regular close, not an after-hours print. Balance sheet and share count are from the 30-Jun-2026 interim (17-Aug-2026), the latest filing. FY2026 guidance (35.4 cps FFO, +4%; 24.5 cps distribution) was reaffirmed at that interim after H1 FFO of 17.7 cps (+5.0%).

historical_growth.eps_basis: FFO per stapled security, NOT statutory EPS: FY2022 32.40c (620.6/1,915.6) -> FY2025 34.0c (3yr); FY2020 28.48c (554.7/1,947.9, COVID-trough base) -> FY2025 34.0c (5yr). Statutory EPS (FY2022 24.5c, FY2023 -12.5c, FY2024 -10.5c, FY2025 51.2c) is revaluation noise and its CAGR is meaningless.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: FFO in A$m: FY2022 620.6 -> FY2025 650.5 (3yr); FY2020 554.7 -> FY2025 650.5 (5yr). AFFO is only disclosed from H1 FY2023, so its only full-year CAGR is 1yr: FY2024 470.0 -> FY2025 494.4 (+5.2%). Per-security FFO from FY2019 (31.5c) to FY2025 (34.0c) compounded at just 1.3%/yr across the COVID and rate cycles.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 FFO guidance (+4.0%, +5.7% ex trading profits, reaffirmed Aug-2026) fading toward the ~2% long-run FFO-per-security record; the base path averages ~3.1% over FY2026-35. Equity CAGR is not used: NTA is a revaluation series.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.5% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+8.2% 3yr) by far more than 30%. The divergence is IAS 40 revaluation (A$770.7m write-down in FY2024, A$310.0m write-up in FY2025), not operating performance; growth is taken from the FFO series instead.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGR overstates operating growth: FY2020 is a COVID base (rent relief) and FY2023-25 revenue includes acquisitions (Grosvenor Place 50%, Highpoint 25%) funded by debt, so the per-security FFO record (1.3-1.6%/yr) is the honest organic figure. AFFO grew faster than FFO in FY2025 (+5.2% vs +5.5%; capex +6.7%) -- maintenance and leasing capex is rising with office incentives and is the axis the bear case works on.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = the reaffirmed 35.4 cps FFO guidance (+4.0% on a flat security count; H1 delivered +5.0% including a lower trading-profit contribution). FY2027 holds 4% on Grosvenor Place lease-up (70.6% occupied at Jun-26) plus 5%-ish logistics like-for-like NPI and funds-management fee growth on A$27.6bn third-party AUM, then fades to 2.5% -- CPI-linked retail/logistics rent reviews with no cap-rate-driven multiple expansion assumed.
base.margin_rationale: FFO / revenue held at the FY2025 actual 63.0% (FY2024 62.3%). This is post net finance costs and post management-company tax. Flat = higher-margin funds-management fees and office lease-up offset by the finance-cost drift as A$5.5bn of borrowings reprice (net finance costs +7.0% in FY2025 vs FFO +5.5%).
base.capex_rationale: Maintenance and leasing capex (the FFO-to-AFFO bridge) at 15.3% of revenue: FY2025 156.1/1,031.9 = 15.1%, FY2024 146.3/988.7 = 14.8%, H1 FY2026 75.4 (+16% YoY) on office incentives. Gives FY2026E AFFO ~A$512m / 26.7 cps (+3.4%), 1.09x cover of the 24.5 cps distribution -- consistent with H1 FY2026 AFFO of 263.4 (+2.3%). Development capex on the logistics pipeline is growth capital funded within the 25-35% gearing range and is what the growth path pays for.
base.tax_rationale: Zero because FFO is already after the management company's income tax (A$15.8m FY2025, A$16.7m cash paid); the trust itself is a flow-through and does not pay tax.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 2.5% = 15.8x terminal AFFO (a 6.3% AFFO yield) binds below the 18x cap. GPT itself trades at ~17.5x FY2025 AFFO today.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 beats guidance as it did twice in FY2025 (5.5%); Grosvenor Place and 51 Flinders Lane lease to >95% by FY2028; the RBA resumes easing so trading profits and transaction fees return; the funds platform keeps raising (A$500m GWSCF raise in 2025 repeated) so fee income compounds at high single digits.
bull.margin_rationale: FFO margin drifts up 1.5pp as capital-light fee income grows faster than rent and lower rates cut the cost of the floating/refinanced book.
bull.capex_rationale: Office incentives normalise once the two big towers are leased; maintenance/leasing capex eases toward the FY2024 ratio.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 3.0% = 17.2x, still inside the 18x cap. Same 9.0% cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows, not a cheaper discount rate.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands a point under guidance (H1 is banked). Then a rates-and-office shock: the RBA's restrictive 2026 stance persists, Grosvenor Place lease-up stalls, office cap rates expand again as in FY2024 (A$770.7m write-down), trading profits vanish and gearing drifts to the top of the 25-35% range, forcing asset sales that shrink the rent base. Growth settles at 1.5%, below CPI.
bear.margin_rationale: FFO margin gives up 2pp as hedges roll onto higher fixed rates and finance costs keep growing faster than income (FY2025: +7.0% vs +5.5%).
bear.capex_rationale: Leasing incentives and maintenance capex rise toward 16.5% of revenue as office tenants demand larger incentives to commit; AFFO cover of the distribution falls below 1.0x by FY2028.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 1.5% = 13.5x binds just under the 14x cap (a 7.4% exit AFFO yield, where the sector traded through 2022-24).

scenario_narratives.base: GPT delivers the reaffirmed FY2026 guidance (35.4 cps FFO, 24.5 cps distribution) and then compounds FFO at 3-4% for three years as Grosvenor Place leases up, logistics rents keep re-rating on 20%+ spreads and the A$27.6bn third-party platform grows fees, before fading to a CPI-like 2.5%. Maintenance and leasing capex stays ~15% of revenue so AFFO covers the distribution ~1.1x. No cap-rate compression and no discount-rate relief are assumed: the value is the AFFO stream capitalised at a 9% AUD cost of equity, which is ~0.5pp above what the current price implies.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2025 pattern of two guidance upgrades repeats, the RBA eases from late 2026 so transaction markets reopen (trading profits, development fees), the two Sydney/Melbourne office towers reach >95% occupancy by FY2028, and the funds-management flywheel (Perron, QuadReal GQLT2, CSC, the new value-add partner) lifts capital-light fee income faster than rent. FFO grows 4-5.5% for five years, the FFO margin drifts to 64.5% and office incentives normalise, so AFFO compounds ~5% and the terminal multiple is 17x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Persistent inflation keeps the RBA restrictive, bond yields back up, and office cap rates expand again as they did in FY2024; Grosvenor Place stays two-thirds leased, incentives rise, and the A$5.5bn debt book reprices higher as hedges roll. GPT sells assets to hold gearing inside 35%, shrinking the rent base; FFO stalls at 0.5-1.5% growth, the FFO margin gives up 2pp and AFFO cover of the distribution drops below 1.0x, so the distribution is cut or funded from the balance sheet. Exit at 13.5x AFFO, the 2022-24 sector trough.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates interest-rate sensitivity, macro instability and office structural risk all 'high', an FY2024-style office write-down happened within the last three years, the flagship acquisition is 70% leased, and net finance costs are growing faster than FFO. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (rates easing, two big office lease-ups, continued fund inflows, trading profits returning). Base 50%: guidance is reaffirmed with H1 in hand and the retail/logistics 98-99%-occupied book is contractual income.

valuation_philosophy.summary: GPT is valued as a stream of AFFO (FFO less maintenance and leasing capex) capitalised at a 9.0% AUD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because AFFO is already after the A$220m/yr net finance cost. Statutory earnings, book-value growth and reported free cash flow are all set aside: the first two are IAS 40 revaluation series and the third includes growth development capex. The base case is essentially the reaffirmed FY2026 guidance fading to CPI growth; it lands a few percent below the current price, which means the market is capitalising GPT at roughly an 8.5% cost of equity versus the house 9%. NTA of A$5.61 is a cross-check, not a floor: the 0.80x price/NTA discount is the gap between the valuers' 5.4-6.3% cap rates and an equity investor's required return once 31.5% gearing, corporate costs and ~A$160m/yr of capex are charged.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: every 50bp on the cost of equity moves the base value ~8-9% because the terminal value is ~55% of it; the price already implies ~8.5%.
Office (43% of directly-owned AUM): Grosvenor Place lease-up from 70.6% and renewed cap-rate expansion are the two ways FY2026-28 FFO growth and the NTA cross-check both fail at once.
Finance costs: A$5.5bn of borrowings repricing as hedges roll; FY2025 net finance costs grew 7.0% against 5.5% FFO growth.
Maintenance and leasing capex: the FFO-to-AFFO bridge grew 6.7% in FY2025 and 16% in H1 FY2026; AFFO cover of the 24.5 cps distribution is only ~1.1x.
Revenue is the driver line, not the valued flow: a change in revenue mix (development revenue, trading profits) can move the FFO/revenue margin without changing FFO.
